title: Longest Non-Decreasing Subarray After Replacing at Most One Element
summary: Given an integer array, determine the maximum length of a non-decreasing subarray that can be achieved by replacing at most one element with any integer of your choice.
statement: Given an integer array, determine the maximum length of a non-decreasing subarray that can be achieved by replacing at most one element with any integer of your choice.
constraints: nums contains one to 100,000 signed integers.
Replace at most one element by any integer.
Return the maximum length of a contiguous nondecreasing subarray.
hints: Precompute the nondecreasing run ending at every index and starting at every index.
Replacing position i can join its left and right runs exactly when the neighboring values leave some value between them.
Otherwise attach the replacement only to the better side; also retain the best unchanged run.
These are all possibilities for a subarray using zero or one replacement, and the two run arrays give their exact lengths.
editorial: These are all possibilities for a subarray using zero or one replacement, and the two run arrays give their exact lengths.

tests.explanation: Replacing the fourth value by three creates a nondecreasing prefix of length four.
The entire array is already nondecreasing, so its length five is optimal.
